earliestResponsibleBranch.trace: segmentSourceUnits splits at the colon, leaving the quoted covenant as its own unit -> no inventory span covers it -> classifyUnaccountedFragment runs -> the quoted-label branch fires FIRST, before contentWords or any caption rule. Nothing earlier in the pipeline touches quotes; segmentation only declines to split inside them. This is the first and only branch that gives the quoted proposition an accounted disposition.

rootCause: DEFINED_TERM_LABEL_RE was /^\s*[“"][^”"]{1,120}[”"]\s*(?:means|shall\s+mean|has\s+the\s+meaning[^.]*)?\s*[.:;,]?\s*$/i - it decided label-hood from DELIMITERS plus a LENGTH CEILING and never looked at what the quotes contained. Any quoted run of at most 120 characters standing alone in a segment qualified, complete sentences included. Quotation marks were treated as proof that source is non-semantic.

genericRuleImplemented.invariant: QUOTATION MARKS DO NOT MAKE SOURCE NON-SEMANTIC. Quoted source is accountable exactly like unquoted source unless label-hood is positively established.
genericRuleImplemented.split: The regex is now QUOTED_LABEL_FRAME_RE and matches only the quote FRAME, capturing the interior. The decision moved into isQuotedTermName(interior), a positive structural test.
isQuotedTermName: 1. No clause punctuation inside the quotes (. ; : ! ? ,). A sentence terminator or a comma is sentence structure; a name has none.

2. Every word inside is either pure grammar (the existing FUNCTION_WORDS closed class) or an orthographic proper-noun form, and at least one is a name. A proposition fails on its predicate: a lowercase content word such as 'make', 'deliver' or 'continuing' is a verb doing work, not part of a name.
genericRuleImplemented.conservativeDefault: Anything not established as a name keeps UNACCOUNTED_SOURCE. False review is acceptable; silent disappearance of quoted operative text is not.
whatItIsNot: no length ceiling - the 120-character limit is gone
no amendment vocabulary: 'amended and restated', 'hereby amended', 'read as follows', 'deleted and replaced' appear nowhere in the implementation
no section-number or issuer or document template
the attack fixture and the generic control are both caught by the same two structural criteria, and the generic control contains no legal vocabulary at all
genericRuleImplemented.acceptedFalseReviews: A lowercase defined term ("business day") and a term carrying internal periods ("U.S. Government Securities") are now reported rather than dismissed. Documented in the function's own docstring; per §6 this is the correct direction of error.
